p:cNvPr.descr: The molecule of arachidonate is at the top of the diagram, labeled below. It has a hairpin-like structure, with the open end facing right and the closed end at the left. The word "up" here is used to describe the zigzag structure of the molecule. The carbons are numbered. Beginning at the top carbon on the open end, there is an O- which bonds left to C1, double bonds up to O and left to C2, which bonds left to C3, which bonds left to C4 with no susbtituents. C4 bonds left to C5, which double bonds left to C6, which bonds left to C7, which bonds down and left to C8. The C4-C5 and C7-C8 bonds are more obtuse than the others. C8 double bonds up and left to C9, which bonds down and left to C10. C10 bonds down and right to C11. C11 double bonds right to C12. C12 bonds up and right to C13, which bonds down and right to C14. C14 double bonds right to C15. C15 bonds up and right to C16, which bonds down and right to C17. This pattern continues with no additional double bonds to C20, which terminates the molecule. There is a dashed arrow between arachinodate and prostaglandin with a circled red X. Beginning on the left with prostaglandin E2 (PGE2, labeled below) the structure is similar to that of arachidonate. Beginning at the top carbon on the open end, there is an O- which bonds left to C1, which double bonds down to O. It bonds left to C2, which bonds left to C3 with no susbtituents. C3 bonds left to C4, which bonds left to C5, which double bonds left to C6, which bonds left to C7. The bond between C5 and C6 is flat. C6 bonds up and left to C7, which dashed wedge bonds down and left to C8. C8 dashed wedge bonds down and right to O, and up and right to C9. C9 double bonds up and left to O, then down and left to C10. This makes up the bend in the "hairpin." C10 bonds down and right to C11 which bonds down to OH. C11 bonds up and right to the O that is also bonded to C8, then up and right to C12, which solid wedge bonds down and right to C13. C13 double bonds right to C14. C14 bonds down and right to C15, which double bonds down and right to C16. The rest of the chain continues with no substituents until C20. There is a bond between C8 and C12 that bridges the sides of the bent chain. This is also true for the next molecule over, thromboxain A2 (TXA2). There is also a dashed arrow from arachinodate from thromboxain, labeled with a circled red X. Text between the two dashed arrows reads "NSAIDs." Beginning at the top carbon on the open end, there is an O- which bonds left to C1, which double bonds down to O. It bonds left to C2, which bonds left to C3 with no susbtituents. C3 bonds left to C4, which bonds left to C5, which double bonds left to C6, which bonds left to C7. The bond between C5 and C6 is flat. C6 bonds up and left to C7, which dashed wedge bonds down and left to C8. C8 bonds up and right to C9. C9 double bonds up and left to O, then down and left to C10. This makes up the bend in the "hairpin." C10 bonds down and right to C11 which dashed wedge bonds down to OH. There is an O inside the ring structure that is dashed wedge bonded to carbon 8 and carbon 11. C11 bonds up and right to C12, which solid wedge bonds down and right to C13. C13 double bonds right to C14. C14 bonds down and right to C15, which dashed wedge bonds down to OH and right to C16. The rest of the chain continues with no substituents until C20. There is a bond between C8 and C12 that crosses the structure. To the right is leukotriene A4 (LTA4)(labeled below). Beginning at the top carbon on the open end, there is an O- which bonds left to C1, which double bonds up to O. It bonds left to C2, which bonds left to C3 with no susbtituents. C3 bonds left to C4, which bonds left to C5, which double bonds left to C6, and solid bonds down and left to O. C6 solid bonds down and right to the same O that it also bonded to C5. C6 bonds up & left to C7, which double bonds down and left to C8. C8 bonds up and left to C9. C9 double bonds up and left to C10. C10 bonds down and left to C11 which double bonds down and left to C12. C12 bonds straight down to C13, which bonds down and right to C14. C15 bonds right to C12, which solid wedge bonds down and right to C13. C13 double bonds right to C14. C14 bonds down and right to C15. This continues until the end of the molecule at C20. To the right is lipoxin A4 (LXA4), labeled below. It has the same 20-carbon hairpin structure with the carbonyl on the top right, with solid wedge bonded OH on C5 and C6. There are double bonds between C7 and C8, C9 and 10, and C11 and C12. This is the point of the hairpin curve in the structure. There is also a double bond between C14 and C15. The chain continues with just single bonded carbons until C20.
